chapterTitle: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 04
subject: english-9

questions.question: Which of the following words is correctly spelled?
questions.explanation: 'Privilege' is spelled with 'i' in both syllables and ends with 'e-g-e'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:

options.A: Every student and teacher was inspired by the guest speaker.
options.B: Every student and teacher were inspired by the guest speaker.
options.C: Every student and teacher are inspired by the guest speaker.
options.D: Every student and teacher have been inspired by the guest speaker.

questions.explanation: Subjects preceded by 'every' or 'each' take singular verbs ('was inspired').

questions.question: Identify the conditional sentence: 'If you heat ice, it melts.'
questions.explanation: This states a scientific reality in present tense, representing the Zero Conditional.

questions.question: Identify the poetic device: 'The leaves danced across the lawn in the autumn breeze.'
questions.explanation: Attributing the human action 'danced' to leaves is personification.

questions.question: Convert to active voice: 'The mysterious letter was delivered by the postman.'

options.A: The postman delivered the mysterious letter.
options.B: The postman has delivered the mysterious letter.
options.C: The postman was delivering the mysterious letter.
options.D: The postman had delivered the mysterious letter.

questions.explanation: Passive 'was delivered' transforms to active simple past 'delivered'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains a gerund phrase?

options.A: Reading historical biographies expands one's perspective on life.
options.B: She was reading historical biographies last night.
options.C: Having read the book, she returned it.
options.D: She wanted to read historical biographies.

questions.explanation: 'Reading historical biographies' acts as the subject noun phrase of the verb 'expands', making it a gerund phrase.

questions.question: Identify the type of clause: 'Although he was fatigued, he continued solving the equations.'
questions.explanation: 'Although he was fatigued' modifies the main verb by presenting a concession, forming an adverbial clause.

questions.question: Identify the demonstrative pronoun in: 'These are the best scientific journals in the library.'
questions.explanation: 'These' stands alone as the subject replacing the noun phrase, functioning as a demonstrative pronoun.

questions.question: Which transitional word introduces an additional supporting point?
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces additional evidence or points supporting an argument.

questions.question: Identify the adjective of quality in: 'The diligent scholar received full scholarship honors.'
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' describes the inherent characteristic or quality of the scholar.

questions.question: Identify the correct preposition: 'She has been studying in this academy ___ 2023.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used to denote a specific starting point in time with perfect tenses.

questions.question: What is the tone of: 'Could you kindly review this draft when you have a moment?'
questions.explanation: The auxiliary 'could' paired with 'kindly' establishes a polite request.

questions.question: In 'The fog comes on little cat feet' (Carl Sandburg), the poet uses:
questions.explanation: Comparing fog to a creeping cat without using 'like' or 'as' is a classic metaphor.

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence:

options.A: One of my best friends lives in Islamabad.
options.B: One of my best friend lives in Islamabad.
options.C: One of my best friends live in Islamabad.
options.D: One of my best friend live in Islamabad.

questions.explanation: 'One of + plural noun ('friends')' takes a singular verb ('lives').

questions.question: What literary element creates sensory impressions for the reader?
questions.explanation: Imagery employs descriptive language appealing to the five senses (visual, auditory, tactile, olfactory, gustatory).
